newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus sees lower interconnect fee.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus sees lower interconnect fee.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd chief executive officer Ziggy Switkowski said on Wednesday he expected the group's connection fees to government-owned Telstra Corp to reduce in the future.
"The charges we pay to Telstra are substantial they are approaching A$500 million a year," Switkowski told the Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) radio.

"We think the charge we are paying to Telstra are still too high and that is sustance of a number of ongoing discussions and we expect to have those resolved in a commercial sensible way over the coming months," Switkowski said.
"The trends around the world are such that the interconnect prices to the monopoly carriers are coming down," Switkowski said. He said Optus was probably Telstra's largest customer.

Optus paid A$409.1 million in connection fees to other telecom networks in the six months ended December 31, 1996, a rise of about 30 percent on a year earlier and its largest single operating cost for the half year.
About 63 percent of Optus' total interconnect fees in the first half of 1996/97 were paid to Telstra and Vodafone Plc, which operates a mobile network in Australia.

Both Optus and Telstra are planning to float on the Australian Stock Exchange this year. Optus' float is being held up by litigation between its associate Optus Vision and one of Vision's other shareholders Seven Network Ltd.
Switkowski said there was a possibility that the timing of both floats could clash. The Australian government plans to sell a third of Telstra through a public share issue.

"It does appear that the Telstra float will be at the latter part of the year, so when our schedule is clarified and indeed when the Telstra schedule is clarified, we will have a look at what that means to us," Switkowski said.
Switkowski said Telstra and Optus, which were Australia's two largest telecom groups, presented different investment opportunities.

"Telstra will be a steady dividend generating investment I believe, Optus Communications position will be that of high-tech, high growth, exciting, perhaps more volatile (investment)," Switkowski said.
"It is not impossible that those floats will happen about the same time, we will see later this year," he said.
Optus earlier reported a net profit of A$58.9 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996, up from A$7.1 million a year earlier.
